messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: getting back histograms
parts:
Hi kind folks-

When i do something like the following example from the
geom_histogram() examples

m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x=rating)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5)
m + facet_wrap(~ mpaa)

I see what I want, the histograms for each mpaa, but how can I get
these histograms back into a data frame or a vector (like a table) so
that I can use them for other purposes?

Thanks,

James

On Thu, Jan 13, 2011 at 16:13, James McCreight <mccr...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Brandon-

There are several ways to look at this. Most plainly, I want the abscissa and ordinates of the plotted histograms... each one of them. They could be in individual vectors or in a data frame, i dont really care. The later would be more "slick", but is not necessary.

I could use table() or hist() but then I have to do all the clumsy subsetting. Why I'm approaching this through ggplot2 is because it clearly makes the histogram calculations over the facet group; a single command is both subsetting and generating the histograms. The syntax for achieving what i want is really easy, a one liner. Doing it manually via other methods seems to take way too much work. 

I'm sure there are certainly multiple ways to achieve this, I'm not tied to ggplot but if i could learn to get the coordinates I desire, that could be useful. I examined the m object and didnt discover what I was looking for.

James

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: getting back histograms
parts:
On Thu, Jan 13, 2011 at 9:29 AM, McCreight <mccr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi kind folks-
>
> When i do something like the following example from the
> geom_histogram() examples
>
> m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x=rating)) +  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5)
> m + facet_wrap(~ mpaa)
>
> I see what I want, the histograms for each mpaa, but how can I get
> these histograms back into a data frame or a vector (like a table) so
> that I can use them for other purposes?

It's not hard to compute the essence of a histogram yourself:

movies$rating_bin <- round_any(movies$rating_bin, 0.5)
count(movies, c("rating_bin", "mpaa")

But for more detail it really depends on what you want to do with the results.

Hadley
